item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Honestly, there are a couple of entries here that drive me mad.

Block of text
Block of text

SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: Powered
Item description: SCP-420-J, exact copy, no changes.
yeah guys, we gotta find a way to un-randomize it, like so we can take things we have taken before… for… um… scientific purposes. - Researcher ██████

First of all, this references a joke scp. I am fairly certain that referencing joke scp's on the mainlist, shouldn't happen. Especially since this one attempts to further the joke. It's why we don't host the joke scps on the mainlist.

Money entered: 9001 Yen
SCP-261 Powered or Unpowered: unpowered
Item Descripton: Kaka Karrot Kakes - Cardboard box with a picture of a yellow carrot cake and a radioactive sign on it. It was tested for radiation, nothing found. D-6217 opened it to find carrot cakes and a sound was produced. It sounded close to the cartoon show "█████████████" The sound was a male human screaming "IT'S OVER 9000!!!" After that, everybody felt energized and full, so the carrot cakes were disposed of.

First of all, why the all caps and three exclamation points? This isn't a note by a researcher this is the formal document. Next the tone, "after that", is just incredibly informal, but then the foundation disposes of the carrot cakes, because everyone felt full? No tests to be done, just "throw it away"? The cakes you didn't have the d-class try?

Some smaller issues aside those points

Notes – Dr. Henjik is a great big baby.

Ah yes, the highest of insults for someone who played food Russian roulette. Despite at the top of the page

Mundane items will be made available for personal consumption after scanning and clearance by Site Security.

Described with a "kill shot", no need for further testing, nope just mundane, let's let the doctor have it instead of a d-class, I'm sure it'll go fine.

Notes – I don't give a damn what they say I scored, that stuff was delicious and worth it for the bottle alone. Isn't there some kind of personalized soda service somewhere? I'm ordering this.

Ah yes, everyone knows that cruel doctors completely ignore the fact they received this from a machine that makes anomalies and most items don't work.


I really needed to get that off my chest.

Tried my hand at a few, with varying levels of jokes and Easter eggs. I made the questionable decision to do so via mobile, so hopefully I didn't miss any typos. I'm a smidge iffy on the coming out cake — I'm decidedly of the 'rainbow cake' persuasion myself and wanted to make a "Comes out perfectly" joke, but I'll understand if it doesn't go over well and gets pruned.

EDIT: Yeah, I have literally no idea why I thought the Coming Out Cake would be funny. The pun was tortured at best and the idea itself was cringeworthy. I wanted to capture the feel of that kitschy rainbow shit you always wind up buying at Pride Festival near the end of the day when you've had way too much junk food and everything seems hilarious, but divorced from that context there was no reason I should have expected it to work. My only excuse was that I was very tired and trying way too hard to do a sequence of gags for which I didn't have quite enough ideas. Removed it myself.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Okay, I know that in general, pop culture references are generally frowned upon by people here, but I have an idea for one, as well as an idea for how to make it work.

Before I start, full disclosure: yes, I'm a brony, and this idea is related to that. But I will try describing it in a way that both fans and non-fans will understand.

In the recent film My Little Pony: The Movie, the character Pinkie Pie is shown using a "Easy-Bake Confetti Cake Cannon", a jumbo-sized cannon that shot out a buttercream cake of questionable quality. My idea here is that a fairly new (anonymised) researcher, known (in-universe) throughout the site as a huge fanatic of My Little Pony Friendship is Magic (a brony, in short), does a test on the machine, which dispenses a product called "My Little Pony: Pinkie Pie's Easy-Bake Confetti Cake Cannon". The product is exactly as it is in the movie, but miniaturised so as to fit through the vending slot of the machine. When tested, it explosively dispenses a low-quality, miniaturised buttercream cake that, when taste-tested, is found to be too sweet and creamy and is judged to be of poor quality. Obviously, the SCP Foundation does research and finds that neither Hasbro or any of its known licensees makes any product like this.

But it doesn't end there. The researcher then reveals in testing notes that not only he himself is a brony, but had watched My Little Pony: The Movie the day prior to the test. He additionally notes that the movie was still fresh in his mind when he conducted the test, and additionally recalls that he may have been subconsciously humming the tune of one of the songs featured in the movie during the test. He then hypothesizes that the machine may be able to "read" the mind and/or actions of its users, and dispenses products as appropriate. As for why the product doesn't actually exist, he additionally hypothesizes that, rather than drawing products from alternate universes as speculated by other researchers, it may, at least sometimes, spontaneously creates products based on what it can profile off the user of the machine, which sometimes may or may not be a product that actually exist.

I welcome your feedback on this idea; if there isn't too much negative feedback to this I will work on it and add it to the article.

item.title: Re: Admin Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Generally pop-culture references don't go over too well because either the reader won't get the reference and will just be confused, or they'll recognize the reference and feel that it's out-of-place among the other more unique entries that don't rely on outside work as a gimmick.

Same kind of goes for the entire site in general. Ideally, the writing we generate here shouldn't depend too heavily on popular things that the author had no part in creating. Borrowing too much from others' work also has the potential negative side effect of making the author look lazy or unskilled.
